title: Broch of Gurness
visualBrief: Specific present-day Broch of Gurness ruins: mapped thick irregular annular masonry and open courtyard, east entrance passage/closed lintel, partly exposed intramural pocket, uneven truncated wall profile, upright stone partitions/shelves/low hearth and covered opening, plus simplified surrounding settlement and enclosure wall remnants. Four existing shared coursed-sandstone/raw-sandstone/gravel/painted-metal graphs. No reconstructed tall tower or roof, furnished prehistoric dwellings, literal inscription/sign atlas, visitor building, whole coastal terrain or invented complete ancient village.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Retained exact-QID OSM way177755139 is the broader settlement envelope. Native named Broch Of Gurness ring52776577268228 supplies an18-vertex outer outline and irregular courtyard hole; named settlement POI35184549843971 corroborates the site. Use native east/south axes/global heading0 at-3.081486977,59.123799747. Ring center[-.672110585,-11.271226264]m and mean radius9.400546m fix the core. The north-up plan and ordinary views support the east entrance, with20degree/2m fine-layout uncertainty. No exact-QID tag on the separate PMTiles ring is invented.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: No retained or native qualified height. Picture-led surviving main wall profile is nominally2.2..3.8m above the bounded courtyard floor; entrance lintel underside1.72m, exposed gallery pocket floor2.05m and peripheral walls roughly0.65..1.05m above coarse native grade. Uneven tops, shelving/slab inventory, settlement linework, gallery condition, hearth and covered opening are approximate visible-remains interpretations, not an excavation survey. No full-height historical tower is reconstructed.
